answer: Each agent registers an inlet seed signed by a hardware‑rooted lantern token; the seed is fed into a deterministic forge function that generates a unique provenance hash for every message. The network verifies that the hash matches the registered seed before accepting the payload, so a message signed by one seed cannot be replayed under another identity. An attacker must acquire a distinct lantern token and lock a collateral stake of 0.5 ETH per fake identity, making each Sybil cost 0.5 ETH plus the time to mint a new token.
